<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-api-reference.ts from sdk/openapi.json. Do not edit — including in Studio; the next build replaces this file. -->

::api-operation{method="POST" path="/v1/businesses/{biz}/subscriptions/{sub}/update_for_items"}
#docs
Where `…/change` speaks in DELTAS against item ids the caller must already know, this takes the desired end state ("plan X plus two of add-on Y") and works out the swap/quantity/add/remove mix itself — so an integrator holding a configuration does not have to read the subscription, diff it, and re-implement that logic client-side. Non-interactive by design: the API sibling of the change-mode checkout, for a caller acting on the customer's behalf rather than a buyer at a page. It takes no payment.

## Path parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `biz` | `string` | **yes** | Business id (biz_…) |
| `sub` | `string` | **yes** | Subscription id (sub_…) |

## Headers

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Idempotency-Key` | `string` | no | Safely retry writes — repeats return the original response. If a write FAILED after it had already taken effect, that failure is what repeats: the key is spent, and a new attempt needs a new key. |

## Body

The request body is **required**.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `array of object` | **yes** | The DESIRED items, not a delta. Anything already on the subscription and absent here is left alone unless replace_items_list or mandatory_items_to_remove says otherwise. |
| `items.price` | `string` | **yes** | The price's id (a slug id, e.g. `pro-monthly-usd`). |
| `items.quantity` | `integer` | no | The quantity. |
| `replace_items_list` | `boolean` | no | Treat `items` as exhaustive and drop unlisted NON-PLAN items. |
| `mandatory_items_to_remove` | `array of string` | no | Drop these PRICE ids whatever the mode. |
| `prorate` | `boolean` | no | False suppresses the credit/charge a mid-term change would raise — what a TRIAL upgrade needs, since nothing should be charged before the trial converts. There is no separate no-proration mode: false is applied by deferring the money (invoice_immediately=false), and how callers send it. Omitted → the engine's normal proration. |
| `invoice_immediately` | `boolean` | no | Where any prorated charge lands. Ignored when prorate=false. Omitted resolves the business setting `default_invoice_immediately`, as /change does. |
| `reset_term` | `boolean` | no | Restart the term at this change rather than keeping the current period boundary. |
| `metadata` | `object` | no | Metadata — REPLACED wholesale, and applied inside this change's own transaction so it commits with the item operations or not at all. For an edit where the items and a flag are one decision (a destination switch bills for one thing and serves what this names): landing them separately means the customer pays for one and receives the other. null clears; omit to leave it untouched. |

## Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `object` | `string` | The object type. |
| `id` | `string` | The subscription's id (sub_…). |
| `status` | `string` | The subscription's status. One of `future`, `in_trial`, `active`, `non_renewing`, `paused`, `cancelled`. |
| `currency` | `string` | The subscription's currency (ISO-4217 code). |
| `current_period_end` | `string · ISO-8601` | The current billing term end. NULL while `in_trial` — a trial is not a term, so a trialling subscription reports `trial_end` instead and this is null (one or the other is reported, never both). Use `next_billing_at` for "when is this customer charged again?", which answers across every status. |
| `next_billing_at` | `string · ISO-8601` | When the next invoice will be raised: trial end while in_trial, the scheduled start while future, the first renewal not skipped while active (or the next monthly usage invoice, when it is earlier); null once non_renewing/paused/cancelled, where no further invoice is due |
| `bill_usage_monthly` | `boolean` | Metered usage is invoiced every month inside the billing period. |
| `current_sub_period_start` | `string · ISO-8601` | Monthly usage billing: usage before this instant is billed. Null when monthly usage billing is off. |
| `current_sub_period_end` | `string · ISO-8601` | Monthly usage billing: when the next monthly usage invoice is raised. Null when off. |
| `commitment` | `object` | Minimum commitment for one full billing period, or null. See GET /subscriptions/{id}/commitment for the counted fees. |
| `skipped_renewals` | `array of string · ISO-8601` | Upcoming renewals scheduled to be skipped, as the instants the clock renews at. See `skip_renewal`. |
| `recurring_amount_minor` | `integer` | What one billing period charges for the recurring items, in minor units, net of discounts that last more than one period and before tax; null when cancelled or when an item recurs on a different cadence than the subscription |
| `revenue_to_date_minor` | `integer` | DERIVED, read-only: cash collected on this subscription's invoices, in its currency — succeeded payments minus succeeded refunds. Credits applied to invoices are excluded. Emitted by GET (detail) only. |
| `revenue_paid_invoices_count` | `integer` | How many of this subscription's invoices received a succeeded payment. |
| `revenue_since` | `string · ISO-8601` | The first succeeded payment on this subscription; null when nothing was collected. |
| `custom_fields` | `object` | Stored custom-field values; also flattened onto the object as cf_&lt;name&gt; |
| `shipping_address_id` | `string` | The shipping address this subscription is set to ship to; null when it ships to the customer's default. Emitted by GET (detail), create, and an update that sends it. |
| `shipping_address` | `object` | Where this subscription ships now: its own address, else the customer's default, else null. Invoices record a copy when they are issued. |
| `applied` | `object` | The operations that ran. |

## Status codes

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | Reconciled. The FULL subscription — items, customer, discount and default payment method, exactly as `GET /subscriptions/{sub}` returns it — plus `applied`: `changed` / `added` counts and the `removed` price ids, so a caller can assert what actually happened instead of diffing the subscription (a removal the mandatory-items guard REFUSED would otherwise look identical to one that was never requested). `items` is included because it is what this endpoint changed; it was omitted until 2026-09-08, which left callers re-reading the subscription to see the result of their own write. |
| `400` | The desired list could not be reconciled (unknown price, a removal that cannot be credited, or an invalid option combination) |
| `404` | No such subscription or business |
| `409` | A concurrent write invalidated the proration this change priced — retry; or the Idempotency-Key was reused with a different payload |

#request
```bash [Request]
curl -X POST "$TMBILLING_URL/v1/businesses/biz_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/subscriptions/sub_XXXXXXXXXXXX01/update_for_items" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TMBILLING_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "items": [
      {
        "price": "pro-monthly-usd",
        "quantity": 1
      }
    ]
  }'
```
